raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old female was referred to our tertiary care ophthalmic center, from AIDS care center for ocular evaluation. Patient presented with intermittent headache for the past 1 month with increasing intensity and vomiting for the past 10 days. The patient was a known HIV-positive person for the past 10 years and on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 8 years. Her CD4 count was 241 cells/mm3 noted at the time of presentation to us. The patient was on zidovudine (300 mg), lamivudine, and nevirapine.
On examination, the patient was stable, anemic, not jaundiced, or cyanosed. Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdomen, and nervous system examinations were normal with no focal neurological defects. Her best-corrected visual acuity in both eyes was 6/6, N6. Cover test showed that orthophoria and pupil in both eyes were equal and reacting to light. Ocular motility was full. Anterior segment examination was within normal limits. Fundus examination of both eyes showed bilateral disc edema with peripapillary superficial retinal hemorrhage and Roth's spots. Optic nerve function tests including color vision and visual fields with Humphrey's perimeter were found to be normal.
Patient was diagnosed as early papilledema with anaemic retinopathy [Fig. 1]. Blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis was done to rule out other neurological illness such as tuberculous meningitis, toxoplasmosis, lymphoma, and cryptococcal meningitis. Lumbar puncture was done and CSF opening pressure was recorded as 300 mm of H2O. Hemoglobin value which was noted as 5 g/dl. Rest of the hematological and hepatic function tests were within normal limits. Neuroimaging of the brain and orbit-magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance venogram (MRV) were done, and they did not reveal any space occupying lesion or venous sinus thrombosis were normal and did not reveal any space-occupying lesion or venous sinus thrombosis. Since the patient was on 3'-azido-3'-deoxythymidine (AZT) based regimen, zidovudine (AZT)-induced anemia was suspected. Based on the above clinical findings and laboratory evaluations, the patient was diagnosed as IIH with anaemia. AZT was stopped and substituted with appropriate ART regimen.
Patient was treated with transfusion of 4 units of packed blood cells along with hematinics and antiedema measures including acetazolamide. She showed prompt, satisfactory response with this treatment and stoppage of zidovudine.
Patient showed signs of improvement clinically. The patient was followed up at close intervals and at 1-month follow-up, there was a reduction in the disc swelling. At the 4-month follow-up, the patient was asymptomatic, and ophthalmic examination showed resolved disc edema and the Hb value had increased to 11.2 g/dl.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old HIV-positive female on zidovudine-based antiretroviral therapy presented with a 1-month history of progressively worsening intermittent headache and a 10-day history of vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who had been living with HIV for 10 years and taking zidovudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine for 8 years, was referred to an ophthalmic center with 1 month of increasingly severe intermittent headaches and 10 days of vomiting without visual loss.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed 10 years prior, on ART for 8 years.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening headache and vomiting. Negative for visual loss or focal weakness. Home medications: zidovudine (300 mg), lamivudine, and nevirapine.

objective.physical_examination: Pallor/anemia without jaundice, cyanosis, or focal neurological deficits; systemic exams normal. Ophthalmic exam showed best-corrected visual acuity 6/6, N6 OU, normal pupils, full ocular motility, normal color vision and Humphrey visual fields, and bilateral optic disc edema (papilledema) with peripapillary superficial retinal hemorrhages and Roth's spots.
objective.routine_investigations: Severe anemia with hemoglobin 5 g/dL; remaining hematological and liver function tests were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was 241 cells/mm3. Brain and orbital MRI and MR venography (MRV) were normal without mass lesion or venous sinus thrombosis. Lumbar puncture showed elevated opening pressure of 300 mmH2O with normal CSF composition and negative testing for tuberculous meningitis, toxoplasmosis, lymphoma, and cryptococcal meningitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of idiopathic/secondary intracranial hypertension (IIH) and anemic retinopathy with bilateral papilledema induced by severe zidovudine (AZT)-associated anemia in an HIV-positive patient, confirmed by hemoglobin of 5 g/dL, CSF opening pressure of 300 mmH2O, normal MRI/MRV, and negative CSF workup for cryptococcal meningitis, tuberculous meningitis, toxoplasmosis, and CNS lymphoma. Treated by discontinuing zidovudine (substituting an alternative ART regimen), transfusing 4 units of packed red blood cells, and administering hematinics and oral acetazolamide, resulting in complete symptom resolution, resolution of optic disc edema, and hemoglobin recovery to 11.2 g/dL at 4-month follow-up.
